status: set from the P22 baseline (see baseline); change a number only with a recorded reason

baseline.measuredOn: 2026-11-22 (P22), commit dc1c237 plus the P22 changes
baseline.environment: Chrome 157 headless, arm64 macOS, Apple M1 Max, 1440 x 900, local static server, no throttling, 5 cold runs per page
baseline.static: Home: HTML 25,240 B gzip, JS 4,730 B gzip, CSS 12,677 B gzip; folder pages at most HTML 4,136, JS 1,608, CSS 12,153 B gzip; the largest image is the Bearnard portrait at 187,394 B
baseline.measured: median LCP 156-252 ms, CLS 0, long-task blocking 0 ms on every page; Home with the nucleus loaded: 543.8 KB of script (raw), LCP 412 ms, 546 ms of main-thread time under software WebGL, 0 idle animation frames
baseline.rule: A threshold is the baseline plus headroom (about 25 percent for sizes, a multiple for the noisy timings), so a real regression fails and run-to-run variation does not. No Lighthouse score is required.

nucleusFrame.what: NUC-050: the median animation-frame interval of the page while the nucleus responds, in the test browser's software WebGL (SwiftShader). It measures the renderer and the machine together, so it has two thresholds that mean different things; it is the median of the medians of several samples, so one slow sample on a shared machine is variation and not a verdict.

reference.applies: The default, and every run on a developer's own machine.
reference.meaning: The standard the nucleus was accepted against (P19): the owner's Apple M1 Max measures 66.6 ms. A frame slower than this on comparable hardware is a regression to investigate.

ci-smoke.meaning: A smoke ceiling for a shared four-core Linux runner drawing the nucleus in software, where runs 2 to 8 of the QA workflow measured 83.3, 99.9, 100.0 and 133.3 ms: it fails a renderer that has become something like twice as slow as the slowest measured run, and says nothing else. It is NOT an acceptable frame time for the site: real visitors have a GPU, and the reference above is the target. The measured distribution of every run is kept in the CI report (qa-report/nucleus-frames.json).

nucleusFrame.policy: Decided by the owner in P22-A01 (D-159): one hardware-dependent threshold could not serve both an M1 Max and a shared runner. Deterministic guards (draw calls, triangles, resources, one canvas, idle rendering, lifecycle) stay exact and are not part of this policy. A failure of this check is a FAIL, never a skip and never a deferral.
